notes: §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR6: "After the execution of the REWRITE statement is complete, the information in the area referenced by identifier-1 is available", with no condition on where identifier-1 lies (2023 adds one for an item inside the file's own records). KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRewrite emits the FROM move into record-name-1, reads the record to send out of the area (SentRecordImage) and passes it to the runtime by value; nothing is stored back into identifier-1 or the record area afterwards. The one store that can follow a REWRITE, EndReleasedRecord, is emitted only when ReleasedRecordNeedsAlsoAvailable finds an out-of-line record in a SAME RECORD AREA group (a dynamic-length or pointer-class record, shapes that cannot be declared at --std 85), so the 1985 path leaves every area as the move left it; the record-name-1 area keeping its content is within "is not available". No edition arm. The witness rewrites from a WORKING-STORAGE group and displays it afterwards. Probed further at --std 85: identifier-1 lying past record-name-1's end in a longer record of the same FD (legal under §1985:IX.4.6.3 SR1, the case 2023 withdrew), with fixed and with RECORD VARYING records, and identifier-1 in a record of another file of the same SAME RECORD AREA clause, each keep their content after a successful REWRITE and after one that fails with status 23.

next.reason: 1985 GR6: after REWRITE 'the information in the area referenced by identifier-1 is available', unconditionally. §2023:14.9.35.4 GR10 adds 'provided that identifier-1 is not one or part of one of the record descriptions subordinate to the file-description'. §1985:IX.4.6.3 SR1 forbids only that 'Record-name-1 and identifier-1 ... refer to the same storage area', so identifier-1 in another, longer record of the same FD lying past record-name-1's end was legal in 1985 and its content guaranteed; 2023 withdraws that guarantee (a result made unspecified). SAME RECORD AREA part via §2023:14.9.35.4 GR6.
